memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: When you enter the land the Lord your God is giving you, do not learn to imitate the detestable ways of the nations there. Let no one be found among you who sacrifices their son or daughter in the fire, who practices divination or sorcery, interprets omens, engages in witchcraft. - Deut 18:9-10 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
As Israel prepared to enter the land, God warned them plainly, do not learn to imitate the detestable practices of the nations already there. He then listed some of them, child sacrifice, divination, sorcery, interpreting omens, witchcraft. These were the dark spiritual practices of people who did not know the true God, and God wanted His people to be entirely different.

Behind each of these practices was an attempt to gain knowledge or power apart from God, to control the future or manipulate spiritual forces on one's own terms. God's people were not to dabble in any of it. They were to trust God alone and seek Him alone.

This warning is not outdated. Our world still offers many ways to seek guidance and power apart from God, horoscopes, fortune-telling, occult practices, and more. These may seem harmless or merely entertaining, but they draw the heart away from trusting God and toward forbidden sources. The New Testament shows believers turning from such things when they came to Christ, even burning their occult books (Acts 19:19). We do not need these dark practices, for we have a living God who guides us by His Word and His Spirit. Are there any subtle occult influences you need to turn away from, trusting God fully instead?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are there occult influences you have treated as harmless?
2. Where are you tempted to seek control over your future apart from God?
3. How does trusting God free you from these practices?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, keep me from every practice that seeks power or knowledge apart from You. Help me trust You alone for guidance and my future. Amen.
